analysis:
Examined the new ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift (head 1-388) and the ProviderLoop+Serve.swift shutdown changes (head 486, 512; base 511-519).

Recovery is local residency management. Its target set is limited to explicitly selected, advertised, eligible models that are not fenced: it requires failedSelfTestHashes[id]==nil and !isRefusedByRetirement (lines 35-42), so it does not re-admit models retired by a self-test or by retirement. Loads go through ensureModelLoaded(allowEviction:false) (line 295), so the existing load checks still apply, including weight-hash verification (T-012/T-027).

Victims cannot be protected models or models that requests could load back (lines 78-81). They must also pass the eviction exclusions and Autopilot victim rules. Each victim is rechecked before unload (lines 119-123, 279), and unloadModel(forEviction:true) can refuse a busy victim (line 284). Recovery pauses during drain, update, Autopilot operations, model switches and other loads (lines 151-163), which limits races with in-flight inference.

No crypto, attestation, authorization (TB-011/T-053), key handling (A-003) or plaintext path is touched. Daemon-state reports contain only model IDs, timings and blocker text, which is non-sensitive and already public via heartbeats.

In Serve.swift, shutdown now includes the recovery attempt task among the cancelled preloads (head 486), so a recovery load cannot outlive shutdown. The base unload loop was replaced by unloadAllModelsForShutdown() (head 512). That helper's implementation is not supplied. Integration should verify that it still waits for modelsUnloading and unloads every slot before powerAssertion.releaseAll(), so slot and KV memory (T-028) and MiMo owners are released the same way as the base loop.

The attemptSelectedModelRecovery checks !isShuttingDown before evicting and loading, but there is a small window between cancel and the load. This is covered by waitForPreloads.

Availability: a provider operator controls local config anyway (TB-003), so there is no new adversarial trigger. No security regression was identified.
